scenario.name: r-cd-return-covenant-authority
scenario.description: Return-covenant authority must survive a real gateway restart. The recipient session's authority generation (the session_recipient_authority epoch) must stay present and unchanged at every sample, including the outage where no process serves, and the transition's bodies and the replacement's output must be retained rather than lost. A generation is usable only while it owns the listener, /readyz passes and hello-ok answers; an unchanged epoch alone is not usability, and continuous service across a restart is not asserted (at F′ the old server closes before any successor is ready). The outage is measured and reported as outageInterval.
scenario.notes: Fixture-gated: k6 cannot start, observe or replace a gateway, so the k6 entry fails closed and the executable control is scripts/run-return-covenant-restart-control.mjs (see the product-path map, with F′ path:line anchors, in scenarios/r-cd-return-covenant-authority.js). The control is the declared external supervisor (OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external) of one disposable gateway that composite-launcher.sh set up and then stopped. It refuses any target that is not $HOME/proof-gw/comp-<sha8> with a matching receipts/identity.json, a stopped openclaw-proof-comp-<sha8> unit, a free loopback port that is not the live gateway's, no channels, and a stage whose dist/build-info.json commit is the candidate. Grading, from the signed record only: PASS-candidate needs all five receipts plus the positive behaviour (old generation ready before the transition; restart accepted; old exits 0 through an accepted full-process external handoff bound to its PID; every sample shows the same authority epoch; the old generation observed serving before the transition and the replacement observed serving from its first serving sample to the end of the window, serving meaning it owns the listener while /readyz passes and hello-ok answers; replacement ready within the deadline with a new PID, socket inode and bootId, both generations reporting the staged buildId; full planned window observed without blind gaps; clean docs harness; cleanup left nothing running). FAIL-candidate when the behaviour is contradicted: authority cleared or advanced, old generation not serving before the transition, no handoff, replacement never serving or not staying served, generations not distinct, or residue after cleanup. Every receipt reports outageInterval (last serving old sample to first serving sample after it, in ms, at one-sample resolution); it is reported, not graded against a bound. MISSING-candidate when there is nothing to judge: no observation matrix, no established authority, or a restart that was never accepted (its failure body is still kept). PARTIAL-candidate when the restart was observed uncontradicted but a receipt or bound is missing (lost transition body, process output, fingerprint, unsigned cleanup, unreadable authority sample, short window, dirty harness). The negative case holds the port with a control-owned socket before the replacement starts. It must grade non-PASS while still showing the old authority and the failure body (negativeControl.holds). The only earlier attempt (historical-baseline-review: zero of 24 observations, no signed cleanup/observer receipt) is not evidence.
scenario.registryNotes: Ledger command AUTHORITY-RESTART-CONTROL, gate reviewed-restart-control-on-final-successor. Rejected base: the first gateway-restart transition cleared the current generation before the replacement became usable, and the exact failure body was lost. The row stays required and MISSING at F′ until this control runs on the final successor (🌊, Discord msg 1565895695586558120).

invocation.transition: gateway.restart.request {reason: gateway.restart, skipDeferral: true} with operator.admin
invocation.authority: sessions.create then session.visibility.set(suggest); the narrowing advances session_recipient_authority
invocation.supervisor: OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external; the control consumes the restart handoff and starts the replacement
invocation.fixtureState: an existing proof-gw directory (composite-launcher.sh setup, then stop); its state is kept for composite-launcher.sh shred

expectedReceipts.name: transition-http-body
expectedReceipts.description: The gateway.restart.request response frame (private verbatim, public redacted, SHA-256 of the canonical frame), plus the /readyz and /startupz bodies at the transition edges: the last pre-transition body, the first not-ready body (draining 503 or refused), the replacement's first ready body, and the last not-ready body when no replacement serves. The rejected base lost the failure body.

expectedReceipts.name: replacement-process-output
expectedReceipts.description: The replacement's stdout and stderr, captured by the control as its supervisor: byte counts and SHA-256 in public with a redacted tail, raw logs in the private directory. A replacement that never serves keeps them as the failure text.

expectedReceipts.name: generation-fingerprints
expectedReceipts.description: Old and replacement process fingerprints (PID, kernel start ticks), each one's listening socket inode and port read from /proc, and the hello-ok bootId SHA-256 and buildId. A replacement that never listened keeps its PID and start ticks.

expectedReceipts.name: observation-record
expectedReceipts.description: The observation window planned before the transition (sample interval, pre-transition samples, transition, readiness and window bounds, maximum sample gap) and the matrix: per sample the phase, the listener owner, inode, owner PID and start ticks, /readyz and /startupz status with a body SHA-256, hello-ok with a bootId SHA-256, the generation observed serving (owner of the listener while /readyz passes and hello-ok answers), and the authority epoch SHA-256. The grade derives outageInterval from it. The baseline attempt produced zero of twenty-four.

expectedReceipts.name: signed-cleanup-receipt
expectedReceipts.description: Cleanup stops only processes this run started (PID, start ticks and run marker re-verified before any signal), closes the negative's socket, and records that no run process or listener remains. The whole observer receipt is HMAC-SHA256-signed (hmac-sha256-proof-observer-key-v1) with a launcher-held key that the gateway processes never receive. The baseline attempt produced none.

review.notes: The control writes a candidate receipt only. Folding it is a reviewed corpus step on the final successor product. The row is not promoted by this manifest and stays MISSING at F′.

liveRunSafety.notes: run-proof.sh and run-proofs.sh refuse orchestration-required rows, so a catalog or live-suite run never fires this control. An operator runs the fixture against a stopped proof-gw gateway: positive case, then the negative. The fixture never reads OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN or OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_WS; it takes the disposable gateway's own token from the proof-gw config. It never restarts, stops or signals a live gateway or any process it did not start.
